title: Austin Trivia Night

questions.q: Austin's unofficial slogan, seen on bumper stickers and T-shirts, urges everyone to "Keep Austin" what?
A huge colony of Mexican free-tailed bats roosts under which downtown Austin bridge?
questions.a: The Congress Avenue Bridge (officially the Ann W. Richards Congress Avenue Bridge)

questions.q: Which long-running PBS concert series, whose pilot was taped with Willie Nelson, takes its name from the city?
What is the nickname of the University of Texas at Austin's sports teams?
Which spring-fed swimming pool in Zilker Park stays cool all year round?
Which music, film and tech festival, known by four letters, takes over Austin every March?
Lady Bird Lake in downtown Austin is a reservoir on which river?
Which US president's presidential library stands on the University of Texas at Austin campus?
Before it was renamed Austin, the settlement on the site was known by what name, shared with a famous battle?
Austin officially calls itself the "Live Music Capital of the" what?

notes: Coined around 2000 by Red Wassenich and popularised by BookPeople and Waterloo Records; see 'Keep Austin Weird' on Wikipedia.
Renamed for Ann Richards in 2006; accept either name.
Pilot taped 1974 with Willie Nelson; see Austin City Limits Wikipedia / acltv.com history page.
Spring-fed pool in Zilker Park, around 68-70F year round; see City of Austin Parks and Recreation (austintexas.gov).
SXSW held each March since 1987; see sxsw.com and SXSW Wikipedia.
Lady Bird Lake (formerly Town Lake) is a reservoir on the Colorado River of Texas; see Lady Bird Lake Wikipedia / City of Austin.
LBJ Presidential Library, on the UT Austin campus; see lbjlibrary.org.
Settlement of Waterloo chosen as capital site in 1839 and renamed Austin after Stephen F. Austin; see Texas State Historical Association Handbook of Texas, 'Austin, TX'.
City adopted 'Live Music Capital of the World' in 1991; see City of Austin Music & Entertainment Division / Visit Austin.
